title: Do Transaction Prices Reflect Visual Preference? A Diagnostic Study with Multimodal Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.41358v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Existing visual preference evaluation relies on costly human annotations or preference reward models, whereas online marketplace transaction prices are readily available and reflect real purchasing behavior, offering potential low-cost supervision. However, transaction prices conflate visual preferences with non-visual factors such as provenance, demand, and competition, making aggregate accuracy insufficient to distinguish model errors, unreliable price signals, and protocol confounds. To address this identifiability challenge, we introduce MarketImage, a diagnostic framework that identifies when transaction prices reflect visual preferences, where they fail, and whether multimodal language models can recover human-supported visual preference signals. translated_title: 交易价格是否反映视觉偏好？基于多模态语言模型的诊断研究
translated_abstract: 现有的视觉偏好评估依赖于昂贵的人工标注或偏好奖励模型，而在线市场的交易价格易于获取且反映真实的购买行为，提供了潜在的低成本监督信号。然而，交易价格会将视觉偏好与来源、需求和竞争等非视觉因素混杂在一起，使得仅凭总体准确率无法区分模型误差、不可靠的价格信号以及实验协议中的混淆因素。为了应对这一可识别性难题，我们提出了 MarketImage——一个诊断框架，用于识别交易价格何时反映视觉偏好、在何处失效，以及多模态语言模型能否从中恢复得到人类支持的视觉偏好信号。MarketImage 包含三个组成部分：(i) MarketImageArt，包含 266 组六图比较集，附带交易价格和价格盲测下的人类排名；(ii) MarketImageLens，一种保留平局的比较方法……
tldr: 提出了诊断框架 MarketImage，用于识别交易价格何时以及为何能够反映视觉偏好，并检验多模态语言模型能否从交易价格中恢复与人类判断一致的视觉偏好信号。
